defense_analyst.prose: ARI sends five or more rushers on 33.3% of dropbacks [dc1] over 318 plays [dc2], 12th-highest in the league [dc3], and averages 4.4 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Its pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 14.2% [dc5], 25th in the league [dc6], so the blitz is more a change of coverage look than a steady sack threat. Expect KC's protection to face one extra rusher often, but don't assume constant disruption. Opposing pass plays average 0.25 EPA [dc7] and 10.1% of them go for 20+ yards [dc8]. KC's offense produces 0.17 EPA per pass play [dc9] with an explosive rate of 8.9% [dc10] over 327 plays [dc11], so the matchup favors KC's efficiency but not its big-play rate. Against the run, ARI keeps 6.7 defenders in the box on average [dc12] and allows a 42.3% success rate on 286 run plays [dc13][dc14]. KC's run success rate is 45.9% over 220 plays [dc15][dc16]. ARI is not stacking the box heavily, so the run game has room to work. On third down ARI allows conversions on 42.9% of attempts [dc17] over 119 plays [dc18], a middling figure. In the red zone it has allowed touchdowns on 69.4% of drives [dc19] over only 36 drives [dc20], a small sample that still suggests KC's finishing drives are likely to score if they reach the 20.
